name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. The benchmark comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.

creator.name: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
creator.affiliation: CUHK MMLab, SenseTime Research, CPII under InnoHK

citeAs: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li. VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv:2509.22651v1, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from 47 existing datasets spanning audio understanding (speech, sound, music), text-based tasks, and vision tasks. Audio clips featuring natural sounds, music, human speech, and combinations were gathered from 23 audio understanding datasets. Text instructions were synthesized into speech using three advanced TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B). For role-play tasks, 100 distinct roles were selected from RoleBench, with three representative audio clips collected per role. Visual data was sourced from MMMU, spanning 30 disciplines and 30 image formats. The collection process involved extracting diverse visual and auditory inputs, synthesizing speech instructions, and curating multi-modal examples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include 47 datasets: 23 audio understanding datasets (e.g., LibriSpeech, Common Voice, Clotho, AudioCaps, MusicCaps, VocalSound, IEMOCAP, SLURP, VoxCeleb1, Fisher, MELD, AudioGrounding, MUSICA-VQA, TUT2017, AVQA, CochlScene, FMA, RAVDESS, MyST, Nsynth), 22 text and audio datasets for speaking tasks (e.g., RoleBench, STORAL, FollowBench, GSM8K, CommonsenseQA, BIG-Bench Hard, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, IFEval, AlpacaEval, SD-Eval, VocalBench, VoiceBench, SpeechInstructBench, VCTK, JL Corpus), and MMMU for vision tasks.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text instructions were rewritten using Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct to ensure suitability for TTS, converting challenging content such as numbers and mathematical expressions into readable formats. Image references were replaced with descriptive phrases. Multiple-choice questions were rephrased for better readability.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A multi-stage curation process was conducted: (1) Deduplication using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance to remove duplicate questions; (2) Validation to exclude incomplete or unsuitable instances, including entries with corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers (approximately 10% of candidates were discarded); (3) Categorization of remaining problems into 13 predefined task categories based on source metadata; (4) Balanced sampling to equalize category representation. Speech synthesis involved generating audio using three TTS models, evaluating quality with UTMOS Strong (regenerating if score < 3.8), transcribing with Whisper-Large-v3, and selecting audio with the lowest word error rate. In total, 13,471 high-quality speech audio files were synthesized.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For role-play tasks, 100 distinct roles were selected from RoleBench, and three representative audio clips per role were collected to analyze role-specific speaking style and vocal timbre. Text instructions from RoleBench were used for role-play evaluation. No additional human annotation was performed beyond the original source dataset labels.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Speech synthesis: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B. Speech quality evaluation: UTMOS Strong. Speech transcription: Whisper-Large-v3. Text rewriting: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct. Evaluation: gpt-oss-20b for content quality assessment, emotion2vec for emotion recognition, Wespeaker for speaker similarity in role-play tasks.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Code and data will be released publicly. The dataset and code are under an MIT license. The authors maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal, reserving the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The benchmark includes role-play voice imitation and speaker similarity evaluation. To mitigate misuse risks (e.g., identity spoofing, harassment, fraud), the authors prohibit training or releasing models intended to reproduce identifiable speakers without documented consent, require downstream users to implement consent gating and watermarking or traceability of synthetic audio, and provide safety cards describing acceptable use, known risks, and red-team tests for voice cloning abuse.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to advance the development of next-generation AI assistants by providing a rigorous framework for evaluating listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It identifies gaps in current models, particularly in multimodal (audio plus visual) input, role-play voice imitation, robustness, and safety alignment. The authors emphasize strict consent, provenance, and anti-impersonation safeguards to minimize harms related to impersonation, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is primarily in English, with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task, which may not capture the full variability of real user interactions across diverse linguistic settings. Questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect the full richness or fairness concerns of real deployments. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and associated style prompts, which may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset, though sizable (10.5K curated QA items), may be limited in diversity. All prompts and evaluations except five Chinese roles are in English, limiting generalization to multilingual settings. The benchmark evaluates models in an offline, static manner, which might not capture practical deployment factors such as latency constraints, continuous listening, incremental speech processing, barge-in, and error recovery. Video-audio integration and continuous audio-visual streaming tasks are beyond the scope. The evaluation relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring, which may introduce noise and bias. The questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, which might not reflect real-world deployment scenarios.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating and benchmarking AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. It is designed for researchers to better evaluate voice assistants and facilitate future studies in this area. The benchmark is not supposed to be used for training models for cheating. Usage guidelines emphasize responsible use, particularly for role-play voice imitation, requiring consent, provenance tracking, and anti-impersonation safeguards.
